Filed by the **`domain:spec` seat 2** execution seat at `objectstack-ai/objectstack` (seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#18549, `session_01JbZnqu8bt6YqfJsr9vaFb3`), out of the objectstack-ai/objectstack#18159 round, 2026-09-19T09:24Z. ⛔ Not claimed, ⛔ not dispatched, ⛔ no `domain:*` and no priority from me — routing and grading are this repo's triage's.

## The trap — criterion (c)

`packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-quick-actions.requiredPermissions-gate.test.tsx` mocks `usePermissions` with a stub whose `can(object, action)` is `granted.has(action)`.

Six tests pin the renderer's **call shape**. ⭐ Every one of them stays green over a provider that answers the object's `allowRead` bit for the same name. ⇒ **the suite reads as coverage of the gate and is coverage of the call.** A reader — human or agent — takes the green as evidence the permission gate holds; it is not.

## Why it matters right now

The upstream half is a live, published divergence: `record:quick_actions.requiredPermissions` is declared in `@objectstack/spec` as `z.array(z.string())` and described as hiding the whole bar unless the user holds every named permission on the object, while the renderer evaluates it through `perms.can(objectName, name)` — a **closed** permission-action enum, not the ADR-0066 capability set the same word names elsewhere. Measured on the two shipped providers: the backend-backed one resolves an unmapped name to `allowRead` (a capability nobody holds passes for every reader); the role-based one denies the same name to everyone whenever the object carries a permission config.

⇒ These six tests are exactly the pins that would have caught that, and they cannot, because the stub cannot fail the way the real provider does.

## ⚠️ Attribution of the readings

All of the above — the stub's shape, the six pins, and both providers' behaviour — is the **implementer's** measurement in the objectstack-ai/objectstack#18159 round, reported with self-tested legs in both directions. **This seat re-measured only the contract half in `@objectstack/spec`** (the three `record:*` blocks still refuse the key by name) and has ⛔ **not** reproduced the provider or renderer readings. Treat them as attributed, not confirmed, and re-run rather than adopt.

## Standing upstream

The disposition of `requiredPermissions` itself — object actions, ADR-0066 capabilities with a renderer repair, or retirement — is a maintainer decision on the objectstack side, carded as **objectstack-ai/objectstack#19186** with its four-facet analysis. ⛔ This card does **not** ask for that ruling and must not pre-empt it. Fixing the pin so it can fail is worth doing whichever way that lands; ⛔ but if the ruling retires the key, this suite goes with it, so ordering is worth a glance before anyone starts.
